title: Efficient LLM Serving for Agentic Workflows: A Data Systems Perspective (Helium)
technique: Helium: agentic workflows as query plans with LLM calls as operators; proactive prompt/KV caching and cache-aware scheduling (makespan-minimizing operator-to-worker assignment)

optimized_metrics.evidence: find an assignment of calls to workers and an execution order that optimizes the makespan (i.e., wall-clock latency) of the execution.

headline_claim.text: achieving up to 1.56× speedup over state-of-the-art agent serving systems on various workloads.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 5, Table 2, Fig 7 (end-to-end latency of a query batch)
Fig 12c per-request latency CDF (28.3 s to 20.5 s vs LangGraph)
Fig 12c (37.2 s vs 51.7 s for LangGraph)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We evaluate all frameworks using end-to-end latency (total wall-clock time for query batch preparation and execution). For Helium, this includes optimization, scheduling, and processing.
metric_definitions.notes: Batch-level wall-clock latency of a whole batch of workflow queries (offline/batch regime), including Helium's own planning overhead. Effectively batch makespan, not per-request latency.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Since throughput is inversely proportional to latency for a fixed batch size, we report only latency to simplify comparison.
The total token step 𝑇 (𝜎) for a schedule 𝜎 is the token step at which the last LLM call finishes, analogous to the makespan in classical scheduling problems.
metric_definitions.notes: Scheduler's internal cost model: time measured in token steps proportional to token usage; objective is min of the max completion over all calls of all workflows.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Helium reduces the 95th percentile latency to 37.2 s compared to 51.7 s for LangGraph. This confirms that cache-aware scheduling effectively mitigates congestion, preventing the straggler requests that typically degrade total workflow completion time.
metric_definitions.notes: Per-LLM-request latency within the batch; used only as an explanatory analysis.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: end-to-end latency (total wall-clock time for query batch preparation and execution)
metric_definitions.notes: Offline batch makespan of a workflow query batch; includes Helium optimization/scheduling time (added in re-pass).

load_regime: offline batch of workflow queries (fixed batch sizes, e.g. 16); not an arrival-rate sweep
tradeoff_acknowledged: Helium adds planning overhead (query optimization, cache-aware scheduling, TRT construction) that is included in reported latency and is shown to be small.
workloads: agentic workflows combining Parallel, Debate, Map-Reduce patterns (e.g. Trading workflow, MapRed, Debate) on several datasets; baselines vLLM, OpWise, LangGraph, KVFlow, Parrot
extractor_notes: Program-level and batch-level: the metric is total wall-clock time to finish a batch of workflow queries (makespan), which is PROGRAM_JCT in aggregate rather than per-workflow JCT.
